授業科目の概要.科目名称: 日本とインドにおける食文化と学生生活
授業科目の概要.授業科目区分: エリア発展科目/Interdisciplinary Science & Innovation Courses
授業科目の概要.対象学部等: 共創学部/School of Interdisciplinary Science and Innovation

授業科目の目的・目標・履修条件について.授業科目の目的（日本語）: 日本とインドの食文化、伝統食材とその文化的・健康的意義、ならびに両国の学生生活について学び、食、栄養、持続可能性について異文化的な視点から考察する。九州大学とヴェロール工科大学の学生によるオンライン協働活動を通して、異文化コミュニケーション能力、国際協働力、比較的な視点を身につける。また、両大学における学びや学生生活への理解を深め、留学への関心を高めることも目的とする。
授業科目の目的・目標・履修条件について.授業科目の目的（英語）: Students will learn about the food cultures, traditional ingredients and their cultural and health significance, and student life in Japan and India, and examine food, nutrition, and sustainability from intercultural perspectives. Through collaborative online activities with students from Kyushu University and Vellore Institute of Technology, students will develop intercultural communication, international collaboration, and comparative thinking skills. The course will also encourage students to develop greater interest in studying abroad and to learn more about academic opportunities and student life at both universities.
授業科目の目的・目標・履修条件について.キーワード: COIL, food culture, traditional foods, traditional ingredients, student life, intercultural communication, international collaboration, sustainability, Japan, India
授業科目の目的・目標・履修条件について.履修条件: Students should be able to participate in lectures, discussions, and collaborative group activities in English. Students are expected to participate in all eight online sessions except in unavoidable circumstances. Because this is an intensive course involving international group work, active participation throughout the course is required.

授業科目に関する学習相談について.担当教員による学習相談: Students are expected to participate actively in discussions and collaborative activities with students from the partner university. They should prepare for each session by reviewing relevant materials, communicating with group members, and completing assigned preparation for the group project. Students are encouraged to ask questions, share their own cultural perspectives, and respect different viewpoints during intercultural discussions.

head: 授業のテーマ
授業の内容（90分授業＝2時間）
事前/事後学修の内容
rows: Orientation, Food Culture, and Student Life (Dec 2, 16:40–18:10)

Course orientation and student introductions. Students join mixed Kyushu University-VIT groups and discuss food, daily life, university life, accommodation, transportation, customs, and study experiences in Japan and India.
Prepare a short introduction to your own food culture and student life and begin communicating with group members.
Food Culture and Traditional Ingredients in India (Dec 4, 16:40–18:10)
VIT faculty lecture on Indian food culture, regional diversity, traditional ingredients, their cultural and health significance, and related food practices. Q&A and group discussion follow.
Read about one traditional Indian ingredient or food and consider its cultural, nutritional, or health significance.
Traditional and Functional Ingredients in Japan (Dec 9, 16:40–18:10)

KU faculty lecture (Prof. Mako Nakamura) on Japanese food culture, traditional and functional ingredients, food practices, and their cultural and health significance. Students compare Japanese and Indian examples.
Read about one Japanese ingredient or food and compare it with an Indian example
Food, Nutrition, Sustainability, and Student Life (Dec 11, 16:40–18:10)

Interactive session on food, nutrition, preservation, sustainability, and student life in Japan and India. Mixed groups discuss similarities and differences and begin planning their collaborative project
Discuss possible project topics with group members. Collect information and references related to the selected topic.
Collaborative Project Development (Dec 16, 16:40–18:10)

Development Groups select their final presentation topic, develop a question or theme, divide responsibilities, prepare an outline, and receive faculty feedback. Students also reflect on what they have learned about the partner country.
Conduct individual research for the group project and prepare your assigned materials, information, or slides.
Indian Food Culture Activity (Dec 18, 16:40–18:10)
Interactive Indian tea-making activity introducing spices and food traditions, followed by reflection on cultural learning.
Continue work on the group presentation.
Presentation Preparation and Group Consultation (Dec 23, 16:40–18:10)
Groups prepare slides, organize speaking roles, rehearse, check timing, and receive feedback from faculty in breakout rooms.
Complete presentation materials, rehearse your assigned section, and revise the presentation based on feedback.
Final Group Presentations (Dec 25, 16:40–18:10)

Groups give seminar-style presentations followed by Q&A. The course concludes with reflection on intercultural learning, international collaboration, food culture, sustainability, and study-abroad interests.
Prepare for the final presentation
